candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §40 (c. 350 AD)

'And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him' — Athanasius marks the ETHIOPIAN-EUNUCH'S BAPTISM as the DI-§40 canonical-anchor for the Word's-Spirit-empowered missionary-extension to the ends-of-the-earth. The Ethiopian-eunuch is the first-named Gentile-baptismal-recipient in Acts (before Cornelius ch. 10) and the apostolic-tradition that founds Christianity in Aksumite-Tewahedo geography (per Eusebius Hist. Eccl. 2.1.13 + Tewahedo internal tradition). Athanasius — Frumentius's consecrator (c. 330 AD) — was the patriarch who ordained the first Tewahedo bishop, making Acts 8:38 the foundational Athanasian-Tewahedo institutional anchor.
